_doc: Phase 379. One row per item where the nano-ros user API does NOT correspond
to the ROS 2 client library it mirrors. Written by hand; read by
`scripts/api-parity.py --check`, which fails on any non-matching row that has
no entry here.
Key is '<lang>:<normalized item>' exactly as the report prints it, where lang
is one of c / cpp / rust. Run the report to get the spelling; do not guess it.
verdict is one of:
divergence  we changed it and a PLATFORM CONSTRAINT is why. `why` must name
the constraint (no_std, no exceptions, no allocator, no runtime
env, single-threaded transport) -- not a preference. This is the
only sanctioned reason to differ (RFC-0036).
extension   we add it because an RTOS scenario needs it; ROS 2 has none.
declined    ROS 2 has it, we deliberately do not, with the reason.
gap         ROS 2 has it, we should too, nobody has done it. A gap is a
legitimate entry -- the point is that it is written down.
rename      the names differ and OURS is the one that should change. A
rename with no platform reason costs the drop-in claim for
nothing, so these are the campaign's work list.
This file is SEEDED, not complete: W1 shipped the correlator, W2 classifies
the rest. `--check` is deliberately not wired into `just check` until then --
a gate that fails on ~2000 rows from the day it lands is one somebody
switches off. Keys beginning with '_' are documentation and are skipped.
the `<lang>:` rows for its own lane, and `scripts/api-parity.py` merges every
shard in this directory. One agent per lane can write without a rebase
conflict against the others.
SHARDED BY TOPIC: this file holds one stage's rows in ALL THREE
languages, because the campaign closes a feature at a time across every
language. `scripts/api-parity.py` merges every shard here, and
`--self-test` rejects a row whose item belongs to a different stage.

c:context_*.why: rcl splits initialization in two -- an `rcl_context_t` built from a separately-constructed `rcl_init_options_t` -- and threads the context through every entity's init. nano-ros collapses both into `nros_support_t`, which is rclc's `rclc_support_t` name and carries the RMW session INLINE (`_opaque[SESSION_OPAQUE_U64S]`, nros_generated.h:949). The constraint is no allocator: rcl's context hands out a heap `rcl_context_impl_t` and its accessors exist to reach into it, and there is nothing here for them to reach. The useful half lives on `nros_support_*`.

c:get_default_domain_id.why: rcl reads ROS_DOMAIN_ID from the environment at runtime. An embedded backend has no environment (RFC-0036, Domain ID), so the domain arrives through `nros_support_init`'s parameter over a documented ladder -- explicit argument, then hosted env, then the baked default -- with `NROS_DOMAIN_ID_INHERIT`/`NROS_DOMAIN_ID_EXPLICIT_ZERO` sentinels because plain 0 has to stay the UNSET marker (issues 0206/0227).

c:get_zero_initialized_context.why: there is no context type to zero-initialize. `nros_support_get_zero_initialized` is the same idiom on the type we do have.

c:init.why: `rcl_init(argc, argv, options, context)` is the layer BELOW rclc, and rclc's own examples do not call it -- they call `rclc_support_init`, which is what `nros_support_init` mirrors. Declining the lower layer is what makes the C API rclc-shaped rather than rcl-shaped.

c:init_options_*.why: the options half of the same collapse. `rcl_init_options_t` is built, mutated (set_domain_id), copied and finalised before rcl_init consumes it; ours are the two arguments `nros_support_init` takes. Same constraint as the `compile-time-options` signature rule -- there is no runtime options object because nothing negotiates at runtime.

c:shutdown.why: as `rcl_init`: the rcl-layer counterpart. `nros_support_fini` is the rclc-shaped teardown.

c:support_get_zero_initialized.why: as `support_is_valid`: rcl's zero-init idiom applied to `nros_support_t`, which rclc does not provide for `rclc_support_t`.

c:support_init_named.why: `nros_support_init` plus a node name. RFC-0046 makes launch the authority on node identity, and an image that was told its name at boot should not have to re-derive it; rclc has no equivalent because a desktop node gets its name from argv.

c:support_init_with_options.why: rclc's options-taking variant. Same constraint as `compile-time-options`: there is no `rcl_init_options_t` to pass.

c:support_is_valid.why: mirrors `rcl_context_is_valid` on the type we actually have. Counted as an extension rather than a rename because rclc -- the C reference -- ships no `rclc_support_is_valid`; we are adding to rclc, not renaming rcl.

c:support_state_t.why: an explicit lifecycle for the support object (uninitialised / initialised / finalised) so a double-init or a use-after-fini is a returned code rather than undefined behaviour. rcl relies on a zero-initialized struct plus `rcl_context_is_valid`; a device that cannot report a crash needs the state to be inspectable.

cpp:Context.why: rclcpp lets several contexts coexist so one process can host independent ROS graphs, and every entity holds a `Context::SharedPtr`. An image is ONE graph and has no allocator for a context registry, so `nros::init()` initialises the single global one and nothing carries a context pointer. The accessors (`get_rcl_context`, `get_sub_context`, `get_init_options`) exist to reach into that per-context state.

cpp:ContextAlreadyInitialized.why: an exception type, and the freestanding builds are -fno-exceptions (RFC-0018). Re-initialising returns `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` through `nros::Result`.

cpp:InitOptions.why: the C++ face of `rcl_init_options_t`; see `c:init_options_*`. `auto_initialize_logging` and `use_default_domain_id` are runtime toggles for decisions taken at build time here (RFC-0045).

cpp:get_contexts.why: enumerates the process's contexts; there is exactly one and it is not a value you can hold. See `cpp:Context`.

cpp:init.why: ours is `init(const char* locator, uint8_t domain_id [, const char* node_name])`; rclcpp's is `init(int argc, char** argv, const InitOptions&, SignalHandlerOptions)`. Both take two arguments and share nothing else -- the correlator reports this as `arity-only` for that reason. Three constraints at once: no argv on a device (RFC-0045), no runtime options object, and no POSIX signals. What is left is the two things a device must actually be told, named directly.

cpp:install_signal_handlers.why: no POSIX signal delivery on Zephyr, FreeRTOS or bare-metal. rclcpp installs a SIGINT handler so Ctrl-C shuts the context down; an image is stopped by its RTOS, a watchdog or a power rail.

cpp:on_shutdown.why: CLOSED as a gap by issue 0790: `nros::on_shutdown(cb, ctx)` now exists, so the names correspond and the row is arity-only rather than theirs-only. What still differs is the SIGNATURE, and the platform constraint is no allocator: rclcpp takes `std::function<void()>`, a heap allocation per callback, while a freestanding no-STL header takes a function pointer plus an opaque `context` and stores the pair in a fixed-capacity static table (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS`, default 2). The `out` handle parameter is the third argument for the same reason rclcpp returns one -- so a callback can be removed -- but it is an out-param because this API does not throw and registration can fail with `Full`. The PRE-shutdown phase, which is the half a device actually needs, is `cpp:pre_shutdown` here and `cpp:Executor::add_pre_shutdown_callback` in exec.json.

cpp:pre_shutdown.why: `nros::pre_shutdown(cb, ctx)` -- the free-function spelling of the PRE-shutdown phase over the global executor, next to `nros::on_shutdown`. rclcpp has a free `rclcpp::on_shutdown` but no free pre-shutdown form; having only the post-teardown one as a free function would leave the half that matters on a device reachable only through the executor object. The phase itself is recorded on `cpp:Executor::add_pre_shutdown_callback` (exec.json). Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_on_shutdown_callback.why: Removal counterpart of `cpp:on_shutdown` over the global executor. rclcpp spells it `Context::remove_on_shutdown_callback`; we have no `Context`, so it sits beside the free `on_shutdown` it undoes. Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_pre_shutdown_callback.why: Removal counterpart of `cpp:pre_shutdown` over the global executor. rclcpp's removals live on `Context`, which we do not have; see `cpp:Context`. Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_ros_arguments.why: argv filtering, and there is no argv. RFC-0045 resolves boot config from baked values and the board.

rust:Context.why: as `cpp:Context`. rclrs additionally makes the context the factory for executors (`Context::create_executor`) and reads the domain from the environment (`from_env`, `default_from_env`) -- neither is available to an image with no env and one session.

rust:InitOptions.why: as `cpp:InitOptions`; the domain arrives through the boot-config ladder, not a mutable options object.
